# EchoGuard

Camera-free motion and potential-fall sensing with Wi-Fi Channel State
Information (CSI) from two ESP32 boards. EchoGuard keeps your privacy because
it never uses a camera.

> **Disclaimer.** EchoGuard is a hackathon research prototype. It is **not a
> medical device**, is **not medically validated**, and must not be relied on
> to detect falls or summon help. No accuracy claims are made: the heuristic and the
> optional classifier have not been evaluated on held-out real recordings.

## Status

| Milestone | State |
| --- | --- |
| 1. CSI connection: firmware, serial parser, recorder, CLI monitor | implemented (firmware not compiled, see below) |
| 2. Live dashboard: signal processing, motion score, local web UI | implemented |
| 3. Calibration and labeled recording, replay | implemented |
| 4. Heuristic fall detection, alerts, event log, `evaluate` CLI | implemented |
| 5. Simulation mode, export, optional Random Forest training | implemented |

**Hardware integration and firmware compilation were NOT verified here.**
ESP-IDF was not installed on the development machine and no ESP32 was
connected, so flashing, CSI capture and serial streaming have not been tested
end to end. Everything on the Python side was tested against the documented
Espressif format (format fixtures, generated signals and the simulator). See
[Verification status](#verification-status).

## Architecture

```
 ESP32 #1 (transmitter)            ESP32 #2 (receiver)              MacBook (or Raspberry Pi)
 firmware/transmitter     ESP-NOW  firmware/receiver      USB       backend/
 broadcast 100 Hz  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~> CSI callback -> queue  ======>   parser -> buffer -> recorder
 ch 11, HT40, MCS0                 printer task: CSI_DATA  serial   -> processing (motion score)
 MAC 1a:00:00:00:00:00             lines at 921600 baud             -> activity + fall heuristic
                                                                    -> alerts / event log
                                                                    -> dashboard (Flask, 127.0.0.1)
 simulation/ (SYNTHETIC CSI_DATA lines, MAC 02:51:4d:00:00:00) ---> same parser and pipeline
```

* You need only two ESP32s. There is no router, no mesh and no internet at runtime.
* The receiver prints the official esp-csi `CSI_DATA` CSV format, so the
  official Espressif tools also work with it.
* Live serial data, replays of recordings and the simulator all produce text
  lines that go through the same parser, processing, detector and dashboard.
* A Raspberry Pi can replace the Mac as host. It is optional.

## Quick start

```bash
make setup            # or, without internet: make setup-offline
make test
make dashboard-sim    # SYNTHETIC demo, no hardware: http://127.0.0.1:8050/
make dashboard        # real hardware: pick the serial port in the page (or ARGS="--serial auto")
```

## Repository layout

```
firmware/transmitter/     ESP-IDF project (from esp-csi csi_send)
firmware/receiver/        ESP-IDF project (from esp-csi csi_recv)
firmware/flash_helper.sh  guarded build+flash helper (explicit port + confirmation)
backend/                  csi_parser, sources (serial/replay), ports, buffer, recorder, cli,
                          config, processing, activity, engine, calibration, recording,
                          detector (fall heuristic), alerts (alerts + event log), monitor (wiring),
                          offline (offline replay), export (CSV), ml/train_rf (optional)
dashboard/                Flask server (server.py, __main__.py) + static/ offline UI (HTML/CSS/JS)
simulation/               synthetic CSI generator (SimulationSource)
tests/                    pytest suite + format fixtures
data/                     config.json, events.jsonl, recordings/, calibration/, exports/, models/ (gitignored)
```

## macOS setup (host software)

```bash
brew install python@3.11        # if /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.11 is missing
make setup                      # creates .venv and installs pinned requirements.txt
make test                       # runs the unit tests
```

`make setup` prefers Python 3.11 and falls back to 3.12. Python 3.14 is avoided
because binary wheels for some pinned packages may not exist yet. You need internet
only for this install step.

If you have no internet but a local interpreter already has the packages from
`requirements.txt` (numpy, scipy, pandas, pyserial, flask, pytest), build the
venv on top of it without any download:

```bash
make setup-offline                                   # default: ~/miniconda3/bin/python3.12
make setup-offline PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP=/path/to/python3 # any other interpreter
```

Optional ML extras (scikit-learn, joblib) for Random Forest training:
`make setup-ml` (pip install -r requirements-ml.txt).

## ESP-IDF installation (macOS)

```bash
brew install cmake ninja dfu-util ccache
mkdir -p ~/esp && cd ~/esp
git clone -b v5.5.1 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git
cd esp-idf && ./install.sh esp32,esp32s3,esp32c3,esp32c6
. ./export.sh                    # run in every new terminal (or add an alias)
idf.py --version
```

See the [ESP-IDF get-started guide](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/get-started/index.html)
for details. The first receiver build downloads the `esp_csi_gain_ctrl`
component, which needs internet once.

## Two-board flashing procedure

Nothing in this repository flashes automatically. Flash exactly two boards,
one at a time:

1. **Unplug the third ESP32** (the one with firmware you want to keep). Never
   connect it while flashing.
2. Plug in the board that will be the **transmitter** only, then identify it
   (read-only):

   ```bash
   make ports                                       # lists ports, flags likely ESP32s
   esptool.py --port /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY chip_id # chip type + MAC, writes nothing
   ```

   `chip_id` resets the board but writes no flash. Note the chip type
   (`esp32`, `esp32s3`, `esp32c3`, `esp32c6`).
3. Build and flash the transmitter:

   ```bash
   . ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
   cd firmware/transmitter
   idf.py set-target esp32                      # the chip from step 2
   idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY flash monitor
   ```

   It prints a banner (target, channel, rate, MAC `1a:00:00:00:00:00`) and an
   `EG_TX_STATS` line every second. Unplug it and power it from any USB supply.
4. Plug in the **receiver** board only, identify it the same way, then:

   ```bash
   cd firmware/receiver
   idf.py set-target esp32s3                    # the chip from chip_id
   idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash monitor
   ```

   You should see `CSI_DATA` lines and `EG_RX_STATS` once per second. Close
   the monitor with `Ctrl-]` before starting EchoGuard.

#   make setup          create .venv and install pinned requirements (needs internet)
#   make setup-offline  recreate .venv from a Python that already has the deps (no network)
#   make setup-ml       optional: install scikit-learn/joblib for Random Forest training
#   make test           run the unit tests

PY      := $(VENV)/bin/python
PORT    ?= auto
BAUD    ?= 921600
SCENARIO ?= demo
DURATION ?= 0
SESSION ?=

ARGS    ?=

# Online setup: prefer Homebrew Python 3.11, then 3.12, then python3.11/3.12 on PATH.

PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP ?= $(firstword $(wildcard /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.11 /usr/local/bin/python3.11 /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12 $(HOME)/miniconda3/bin/python3.12) $(shell command -v python3.11 2>/dev/null) $(shell command -v python3.12 2>/dev/null))

# Offline setup: an interpreter that already has numpy/scipy/pandas/pyserial/flask/pytest.
# Uses PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP only when it was given explicitly (command line or environment).
ifneq ($(filter command line environment,$(origin PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP)),)
OFFLINE_PYTHON ?= $(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP)
else
OFFLINE_PYTHON ?= $(HOME)/miniconda3/bin/python3.12
endif

IMPORT_CHECK := import importlib.metadata as m, numpy, scipy, pandas, serial, flask, pytest; \
	print('deps OK:', ', '.join(p + ' ' + m.version(p) for p in ('numpy', 'scipy', 'pandas', 'pyserial', 'flask', 'pytest')))

.PHONY: setup setup-offline setup-ml test ports monitor dashboard simulate dashboard-sim evaluate train-rf clean

setup:
	@if [ -z "$(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP)" ]; then echo "No python3.11/python3.12 found. Install with: brew install python@3.11"; exit 1; fi
	@echo "Using $(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP) ($$($(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP) --version))"
	@if [ ! -x "$(PY)" ]; then $(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP) -m venv $(VENV); fi
	$(PY) -m pip install --upgrade pip
	$(PY) -m pip install -r requirements.txt
	$(PY) -c "$(IMPORT_CHECK)"

setup-offline:
	@if [ ! -x "$(OFFLINE_PYTHON)" ]; then echo "$(OFFLINE_PYTHON) not found. Pass one with: make setup-offline PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP=/path/to/python3"; exit 1; fi
	@echo "Using $(OFFLINE_PYTHON) ($$($(OFFLINE_PYTHON) --version)) with --system-site-packages (no network)"
	@$(OFFLINE_PYTHON) -c "$(IMPORT_CHECK)" || { echo "$(OFFLINE_PYTHON) lacks required packages (see requirements.txt)"; exit 1; }
	rm -rf $(VENV)
	$(OFFLINE_PYTHON) -m venv --system-site-packages $(VENV)
	$(PY) -c "$(IMPORT_CHECK)"

setup-ml:
	$(PY) -m pip install -r requirements-ml.txt

test:
	$(PY) -m pytest -q tests/

ports:
	$(PY) -m backend.cli ports

monitor:
	$(PY) -m backend.cli monitor --port $(PORT) --baud $(BAUD)

dashboard:
	$(PY) -m dashboard $(ARGS)

# SYNTHETIC data, no ESP32 needed: make simulate SCENARIO=potential_fall DURATION=12
simulate:
	$(PY) -m backend.cli monitor --simulate $(SCENARIO) --duration $(DURATION)

dashboard-sim:
	$(PY) -m dashboard --simulate $(SCENARIO) $(ARGS)

# Heuristic check on recorded takes: make evaluate SESSION=data/recordings/<session_id>
evaluate:
	@if [ -z "$(SESSION)" ]; then echo "usage: make evaluate SESSION=data/recordings/<session_id>"; exit 2; fi
	$(PY) -m backend.cli evaluate --session $(SESSION)

# Optional (needs make setup-ml): Random Forest with session-held-out evaluation
train-rf:
	$(PY) -m backend.ml.train_rf --recordings data/recordings $(ARGS)

clean:
	rm -rf .pytest_cache
	find . -name __pycache__ -type d -prune -not -path "./$(VENV)/*" -exec rm -rf {} +

"""Guided self-calibration: noise levels, baseline profile and motion thresholds.

Workflow (:class:`CalibrationSession`), each step recorded for a fixed span of
packet time while the engine runs:

1. ``empty_baseline`` - empty, stationary room (15-30 s, default 20 s)
2. ``walking``        - a person walks across the sensing area (default 15 s)
3. ``standing_still`` - a person stands still in the area (default 10 s)
4. ``sitting``        - ordinary sitting down / seated (default 10 s)
5. compute            - :func:`compute_calibration`

A run (:meth:`CalibrationSession.begin`) waits ``lead_in_s`` (time to leave the
room), then records; with ``auto`` the remaining steps follow by themselves,
with ``grace_s`` between the empty room and walking (time to come back in).
:func:`build_timeline` gives the planned schedule shown in the dashboard.

Frames come from the engine thread (``Engine.add_frame_hook``) together with
``SignalProcessor.last_smoothed`` (the normalised, filtered amplitude profile
that the features and the baseline deviation use). Nothing is driven by the UI
refresh.

Computed values:

* empty-room baseline: per-subcarrier mean and std of the smoothed profile,
* noise levels: median / p95 of variance, diff energy, baseline deviation and
  motion score in the empty room; ``noise_variance`` / ``noise_diff`` (medians)
  become the motion-score normalisation, so a calibrated empty room scores ~1,
* per-step distributions (median, quartiles, p5/p95) of the recomputed
  calibrated motion score and other features, and per-step mean profiles,
* preliminary thresholds from the empty/still p95 and the walking median/p95
  (monotonic ``low < movement < rapid``; falls back to conservative defaults
  with a warning when walking is not clearly separable from stillness).

Calibrations are persisted as ``data/calibration/<sensor_key>.json``, where the
key combines placement, chip family, TX MAC, channel, secondary channel and
CSI length. Calibrations computed from synthetic (simulated) data carry
``synthetic: true`` and a ``__synthetic`` key suffix, and are never applied to
real sources automatically (and not manually either).

These thresholds are preliminary heuristics, not validated detection limits.
"""

    StepSpec("empty_baseline", "Empty room baseline",
             "Leave the sensing area (or the room) and keep everything still: no people, pets, fans or "
             "moving curtains between or near the two boards.", 20.0, 15.0, 30.0,
             cue="Stay out of the room. Recording the empty room.", person_present=False),
    StepSpec("walking", "Walking",
             "Walk back and forth across the sensing area, crossing the line between the two boards, "
             "at a normal pace.", 15.0, 5.0, 60.0,
             cue="Start walking back and forth between the boards."),
    StepSpec("standing_still", "Standing still",
             "Stand still in the middle of the sensing area. Breathe normally, do not move your arms.",
             10.0, 5.0, 60.0, cue="Stop and stand still."),
    StepSpec("sitting", "Ordinary sitting",
             "Sit down on a chair in the sensing area as you normally would and stay seated.",
             10.0, 5.0, 60.0, cue="Sit down on the chair and stay seated."),
]
STEP_KEYS = [s.key for s in STEPS]
STEP_BY_KEY = {s.key: s for s in STEPS}

#: Wait before the first recorded step of a run (time to leave the room).
MAX_LEAD_IN_S = 60.0
#: Wait between an empty-room step and the next step with a person (time to
#: come back in). The dashboard defaults both to 5 s.
MAX_GRACE_S = 60.0


def _seconds(value, name: str, hi: float) -> float:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(value) \
            or not (0 <= value <= hi):
        raise CalibrationError(f"{name} must be 0-{hi:g} s")
    return float(value)


def build_timeline(keys, durations: dict, lead_in_s: float = 0.0, grace_s: float = 0.0,
                   settle_s: float = 0.0) -> dict:
    """Planned wall-clock schedule for recording ``keys`` back to back.

    Phases, in order: an optional lead-in before the first step, each step
    (``settle_s`` discarded while the analysis window clears, then the step
    duration), and an optional grace period before the first step with a person
    that follows an empty-room step. Times are seconds from pressing Start.
    """
    phases = []
    t = 0.0

    def add(kind, key, title, cue, length):
        nonlocal t
        phases.append({"kind": kind, "key": key, "title": title, "cue": cue, "start_s": round(t, 3),
                       "end_s": round(t + length, 3), "length_s": round(length, 3)})
        t += length

    prev = None
    for i, key in enumerate(keys):
        spec = STEP_BY_KEY[key]
        if i == 0 and lead_in_s > 0:
            cue = ("Leave the room now." if not spec.person_present
                   else f"Get ready: {spec.title.lower()} starts in {lead_in_s:g} seconds.")
            add("lead_in", key, "Lead-in", cue, lead_in_s)
        elif prev is not None and spec.person_present and not prev.person_present and grace_s > 0:
            add("grace", key, "Come back in",
                f"Come back in. {spec.title} starts in {grace_s:g} seconds.", grace_s)
        add("step", key, spec.title, spec.cue, settle_s + float(durations[key]))
        prev = spec
    return {"phases": phases, "total_s": round(t, 3), "settle_s": settle_s}

#: A step needs this fraction of frames with sufficient data quality ...
MIN_OK_FRACTION = 0.8
#: ... and at least this many good frames (or half the expected frames).
MIN_OK_FRAMES = 20
#: Walking median must exceed the quiet (empty/still) p95 by this factor.
SEPARATION_RATIO = 1.5
#: Minimum relative gaps enforced between thresholds.
MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW = 1.1
RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT = 1.2
#: Floor for the noise references (normalised amplitude units).
NOISE_FLOOR = 1e-6
FEATURES = ("motion_score", "variance", "diff_energy", "baseline_deviation")


class CalibrationError(ValueError):
    """Invalid request, state, or data that cannot be calibrated (HTTP 400)."""


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
def _slug_part(value) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"[^0-9a-z]", "", str(value).lower())
    return s or "na"


def sensor_part(sensor: Optional[dict], synthetic: bool = False) -> Optional[str]:
    """Placement-independent part of the calibration key (None if unknown)."""
    if not sensor or not sensor.get("chip_family"):
        return None
    sec = sensor.get("secondary_channel")
    part = (f"{_slug_part(sensor.get('chip_family'))}_{_slug_part(sensor.get('tx_mac') or 'unknown')}"
            f"_ch{_slug_part(sensor.get('channel'))}-{_slug_part(sec if sec is not None else 'na')}"
            f"_len{_slug_part(sensor.get('csi_len'))}")
    return part + (SYNTHETIC_SUFFIX if synthetic else "")


def sensor_key(sensor: dict, placement: str, synthetic: bool = False) -> str:
    """``<placement>__<chip>_<txmac>_ch<ch>-<sec>_len<len>[__synthetic]``."""
    part = sensor_part(sensor, synthetic)
    if part is None:
        raise CalibrationError("sensor configuration unknown (no CSI packets seen yet)")
    return f"{validate_placement(placement)}__{part}"


def validate_key(key) -> str:
    if not isinstance(key, str) or not KEY_RE.match(key):
        raise CalibrationError("invalid calibration key")
    return key


def _stats(values) -> Optional[dict]:
    a = np.asarray([v for v in values if v is not None], dtype=float)
    a = a[np.isfinite(a)]
    if a.size == 0:
        return None
    p = np.percentile(a, [5, 25, 50, 75, 95])
    return {"n": int(a.size), "min": float(a.min()), "p05": float(p[0]), "p25": float(p[1]), "median": float(p[2]),
            "p75": float(p[3]), "p95": float(p[4]), "max": float(a.max()), "mean": float(a.mean())}


def _profile_stats(profiles: list):
    if not profiles:
        return None, None
    P = np.vstack(profiles).astype(float)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
        return np.nanmean(P, axis=0), np.nanstd(P, axis=0)


def _json_list(arr) -> list:
    return [round(float(v), 6) if v is not None and math.isfinite(v) else None for v in np.asarray(arr, dtype=float)]


def _to_array(values) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.array([np.nan if v is None else v for v in values], dtype=float)


# -------------------------------------------------------------- step data
@dataclass
class StepData:
    key: str
    duration_s: float
    status: str = "pending"            # pending | recording | done | failed
    failure: Optional[str] = None
    settle_s: float = 0.0              # frames in the first settle_s are skipped (window still holds the previous step)
    t0: Optional[float] = None
    t0_hint: Optional[float] = None    # packet time the step starts at when chained directly to the previous one    t_last: Optional[float] = None
    wall_start: Optional[float] = None
    total: int = 0
    ok: int = 0
    reasons: Counter = field(default_factory=Counter)
    features: dict = field(default_factory=lambda: {k: [] for k in FEATURES})
    profiles: list = field(default_factory=list)
    layout: Optional[tuple] = None
    sensor: Optional[dict] = None
    synthetic: Optional[bool] = None
    source_kind: Optional[str] = None
    problems: list = field(default_factory=list)
    last_quality: Optional[dict] = None

    @property
    def elapsed_s(self) -> float:
        if self.t0 is None or self.t_last is None:
            return 0.0
        return max(0.0, self.t_last - self.t0 - self.settle_s)

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        spec = STEP_BY_KEY[self.key]
        return {
            "key": self.key, "title": spec.title, "instructions": spec.instructions,
            "duration_s": self.duration_s, "status": self.status, "failure": self.failure,
            "elapsed_s": round(self.elapsed_s, 2), "frames": self.total, "ok_frames": self.ok,
            "ok_fraction": round(self.ok / self.total, 3) if self.total else None,
            "top_reasons": [{"reason": r, "count": c} for r, c in self.reasons.most_common(3)],
            "last_quality": self.last_quality,
        }


def step_problems(sd: StepData, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0) -> list:
    """Reasons why a step's data is insufficient (empty list = OK)."""
    problems = list(sd.problems)
    if sd.total == 0:
        return problems + ["no motion frames were received (is a data source running?)"]
    frac = sd.ok / sd.total
    min_ok = max(MIN_OK_FRAMES, int(0.5 * sd.duration_s * max(frame_rate_hz, 1.0)))
    top = ", ".join(f"{r} x{c}" for r, c in sd.reasons.most_common(3))
    if frac < MIN_OK_FRACTION:
        problems.append(f"only {frac:.0%} of frames had sufficient data quality (need {MIN_OK_FRACTION:.0%})"
                        + (f"; main reasons: {top}" if top else ""))
    if sd.ok < min_ok:
        problems.append(f"only {sd.ok} frames with sufficient quality (need at least {min_ok})")
    if sd.elapsed_s < 0.9 * sd.duration_s:
        problems.append(f"covered {sd.elapsed_s:.1f} s of {sd.duration_s:g} s")
    if sd.key == "empty_baseline" and len(sd.profiles) < min_ok:
        problems.append("not enough amplitude profiles for the baseline")
    return problems


# --------------------------------------------------------------- compute
def compute_calibration(steps: dict, placement: str, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0,
                        defaults: Optional[MotionThresholds] = None, now: Optional[float] = None) -> dict:
    """Derive baseline, noise levels and thresholds from recorded steps.

    ``steps`` maps step keys to :class:`StepData`. Raises
    :class:`CalibrationError` (with every reason) when a step is missing or its
    data quality was insufficient.
    """
    defaults = defaults or MotionThresholds()
    problems = []
    for key in STEP_KEYS:
        sd = steps.get(key)
        if sd is None or sd.total == 0:
            problems.append(f"{STEP_BY_KEY[key].title}: not recorded")
            continue
        for p in step_problems(sd, frame_rate_hz):
            problems.append(f"{STEP_BY_KEY[key].title}: {p}")
    if problems:
        raise CalibrationError("cannot compute calibration: " + "; ".join(problems))

    empty = steps["empty_baseline"]
    layouts = {steps[k].layout for k in STEP_KEYS}
    if len(layouts) != 1:
        raise CalibrationError("cannot compute calibration: the CSI layout differs between steps")
    warnings_out = []

    ev = np.asarray(empty.features["variance"], dtype=float)
    ed = np.asarray(empty.features["diff_energy"], dtype=float)
    noise_variance = float(np.median(ev))
    noise_diff = float(np.median(ed))
    if noise_variance < NOISE_FLOOR or noise_diff < NOISE_FLOOR:
        warnings_out.append("empty-room noise is essentially zero; noise references were floored "
                            f"at {NOISE_FLOOR:g} (is the signal real and varying?)")
    noise_variance = max(noise_variance, NOISE_FLOOR)
    noise_diff = max(noise_diff, NOISE_FLOOR)

    base_mean, base_std = _profile_stats(empty.profiles)

    def deviation(profile):
        ok = np.isfinite(profile) & np.isfinite(base_mean) & np.isfinite(base_std)
        if not ok.any():
            return None
        return float(np.mean(np.abs(profile[ok] - base_mean[ok]) / np.maximum(base_std[ok], STD_FLOOR)))

    step_out = {}
    scores = {}
    for key in STEP_KEYS:
        sd = steps[key]
        v = np.asarray(sd.features["variance"], dtype=float)
        d = np.asarray(sd.features["diff_energy"], dtype=float)
        s = 0.5 * (v / noise_variance + d / noise_diff)
        scores[key] = s
        devs = [deviation(p) for p in sd.profiles]
        pm, ps = _profile_stats(sd.profiles)
        step_out[key] = {
            "title": STEP_BY_KEY[key].title,
            "duration_s": sd.duration_s,
            "elapsed_s": round(sd.elapsed_s, 2),
            "frames": sd.total,
            "ok_frames": sd.ok,
            "ok_fraction": round(sd.ok / sd.total, 3),
            "stats": {
                "motion_score": _stats(s.tolist()),
                "variance": _stats(sd.features["variance"]),
                "diff_energy": _stats(sd.features["diff_energy"]),
                "baseline_deviation": _stats(devs),
                "motion_score_uncalibrated": _stats(sd.features["motion_score"]),
            },
            "profile_mean": _json_list(pm) if pm is not None else [],
            "profile_std": _json_list(ps) if ps is not None else [],
        }

    q = lambda key, pct: float(np.percentile(scores[key], pct))  # noqa: E731
    quiet_p95 = max(q("empty_baseline", 95), q("standing_still", 95))
    walk_med = q("walking", 50)
    walk_p95 = q("walking", 95)
    separable = walk_med >= SEPARATION_RATIO * quiet_p95
    if separable:
        gap = walk_med - quiet_p95
        low = quiet_p95 + 0.25 * gap
        movement = quiet_p95 + 0.5 * gap
        rapid = max(1.5 * walk_p95, 2.0 * movement)
    else:
        warnings_out.append(
            f"walking is not clearly separable from the empty room / standing still (walking median "
            f"{walk_med:.2f} vs quiet p95 {quiet_p95:.2f}, need x{SEPARATION_RATIO:g}); using conservative "
            "default thresholds. Check the board placement and that the person crossed the line between "
            "the boards, then recalibrate.")
        low = max(defaults.low, 1.2 * quiet_p95)
        movement = max(defaults.movement, 1.5 * low)
        rapid = max(defaults.rapid, 2.0 * movement)
    if movement < MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW * low:
        movement = MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW * low
        warnings_out.append("movement threshold raised to keep it above the stillness threshold")
    if rapid < RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT * movement:
        rapid = RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT * movement
        warnings_out.append("rapid threshold raised to keep it above the movement threshold")
    if q("sitting", 50) >= rapid:
        warnings_out.append("ordinary sitting scored above the rapid-movement threshold; rapid movement may be "
                            "flagged during normal sitting")

    now = time.time() if now is None else now
    noise = {f: step_out["empty_baseline"]["stats"][f] for f in ("variance", "diff_energy", "baseline_deviation")}
    noise["motion_score"] = step_out["empty_baseline"]["stats"]["motion_score"]
    family, width = empty.layout
    synthetic = any(bool(steps[k].synthetic) for k in STEP_KEYS)
    return {
        "format": CALIBRATION_FORMAT,
        "kind": "echoguard-calibration",
        "placement": validate_placement(placement),
        "created": iso(now),
        "created_unix": now,
        "app_version": __version__,
        "source_kind": empty.source_kind,
        "synthetic": synthetic,
        "sensor": empty.sensor,
        "durations": {k: steps[k].duration_s for k in STEP_KEYS},
        "baseline": {"chip_family": family, "n_subcarriers": width,
                     "mean_profile": _json_list(base_mean), "std_profile": _json_list(base_std)},
        "noise_variance": noise_variance,
        "noise_diff": noise_diff,
        "noise": noise,
        "thresholds": {"low": round(low, 4), "movement": round(movement, 4), "rapid": round(rapid, 4),
                       "calibrated": True},
        "separable": bool(separable),
        "quiet_p95": quiet_p95,
        "walking_median": walk_med,
        "walking_p95": walk_p95,
        "warnings": warnings_out,
        "steps": step_out,
        "note": "Preliminary heuristic thresholds from one calibration run; not validated detection limits.",
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------- session
class CalibrationSession:
    """State machine for one guided calibration. Not thread-safe by itself
    (the :class:`CalibrationManager` holds a lock around every call).

    :meth:`begin` starts a run: after ``lead_in_s`` (wall clock) the current
    step records; with ``auto`` the remaining steps follow on their own, with
    ``grace_s`` before the first step with a person after the empty room (time
    to come back in) and no pause otherwise. A failed step stops the run.
    """

    def __init__(self, placement: str, durations: Optional[dict] = None, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0,
                 clock=time.time, defaults: Optional[MotionThresholds] = None, settle_s: float = 1.0,
                 lead_in_s: float = 0.0, grace_s: float = 0.0, auto: bool = False) -> None:
        self.placement = validate_placement(placement)
        self.frame_rate_hz = float(frame_rate_hz)
        self.settle_s = max(0.0, float(settle_s))
        self.lead_in_s = _seconds(lead_in_s, "lead-in", MAX_LEAD_IN_S)
        self.grace_s = _seconds(grace_s, "grace period", MAX_GRACE_S)
        if not isinstance(auto, bool):
            raise CalibrationError("auto must be true or false")
        self.auto = auto
        self.clock = clock
        self.defaults = defaults
        durations = durations or {}
        if not isinstance(durations, dict):
            raise CalibrationError("durations must be an object")
        unknown = set(durations) - set(STEP_KEYS)
        if unknown:
            raise CalibrationError(f"unknown calibration steps: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
        self.steps = {}
        for spec in STEPS:
            d = durations.get(spec.key, spec.default_s)
            if isinstance(d, bool) or not isinstance(d, (int, float)) or not (spec.min_s <= d <= spec.max_s):
                raise CalibrationError(f"{spec.title} duration must be {spec.min_s:g}-{spec.max_s:g} s")
            self.steps[spec.key] = StepData(spec.key, float(d))
        self.state = "ready"           # ready | waiting | recording | computed | failed | cancelled
        self.step_index = 0
        self.result: Optional[dict] = None
        self.error: Optional[str] = None
        self.created = clock()
        self.running = False           # a run started with begin() is in progress
        self.run_keys: list = []       # steps planned for the current run
        self.run_started: Optional[float] = None
        self.wait_until: Optional[float] = None
        self.wait_kind: Optional[str] = None   # lead_in | grace

    @property
    def current(self) -> Optional[StepData]:
        if 0 <= self.step_index < len(STEPS):
            return self.steps[STEP_KEYS[self.step_index]]
        return None

    def planned_keys(self) -> list:
        """Steps a run started now would record (all pending ones with auto)."""
        cur = self.current
        if cur is None:
            return []
        if not self.auto:
            return [cur.key]
        return [k for k in STEP_KEYS[self.step_index:] if k == cur.key or self.steps[k].status != "done"]

    def timeline(self) -> dict:
        keys = self.run_keys if self.running else self.planned_keys()
        return build_timeline(keys, {k: self.steps[k].duration_s for k in STEP_KEYS},
                              self.lead_in_s, self.grace_s, self.settle_s)

    def begin(self) -> None:
        """Start a run: lead-in, then the current step (and the rest with auto)."""
        if self.state != "ready" or self.current is None:
            raise CalibrationError(f"cannot start a step in state '{self.state}'")
        self.run_keys = self.planned_keys()
        self.run_started = self.clock()
        self.running = True
        self._schedule(self.lead_in_s, "lead_in")

    def start_step(self) -> None:
        """Record the current step immediately (no lead-in, no auto-advance)."""
        if self.state != "ready" or self.current is None:
            raise CalibrationError(f"cannot start a step in state '{self.state}'")
        self._start_current()

    def _schedule(self, delay: float, kind: str, t0_hint: Optional[float] = None) -> None:
        if delay > 0:
            self.state = "waiting"
            self.wait_until = self.clock() + delay
            self.wait_kind = kind
        else:
            self._start_current(t0_hint)

    def _start_current(self, t0_hint: Optional[float] = None) -> None:
        sd = self.current
        self.steps[sd.key] = StepData(sd.key, sd.duration_s, status="recording", wall_start=self.clock(),
                                      settle_s=self.settle_s, t0_hint=t0_hint)
        self.state = "recording"
        self.wait_until = None
        self.wait_kind = None

    def tick(self) -> None:
        """Start the scheduled step once its lead-in / grace period is over."""
        if self.state == "waiting" and self.clock() >= self.wait_until:
            self._start_current()

    def add_frame(self, frame, profile, layout, sensor=None, synthetic=None, source_kind=None) -> None:
        """Engine thread: one motion frame plus the current smoothed profile."""
        self.tick()
        if self.state != "recording":
            return
        sd = self.current
        if sd.t0 is None:
            sd.t0 = sd.t0_hint if sd.t0_hint is not None and sd.t0_hint <= frame.ts else frame.ts
            sd.layout = layout
            sd.sensor, sd.synthetic, sd.source_kind = sensor, synthetic, source_kind
            ref = self.steps["empty_baseline"]
            if sd.key != "empty_baseline" and ref.status == "done":
                if layout != ref.layout or (sensor_part(sensor) != sensor_part(ref.sensor)) or synthetic != ref.synthetic:
                    sd.problems.append("the sensor configuration or source differs from the empty-room baseline")
                    self._finish_step()
                    return
        elif layout != sd.layout:
            sd.problems.append("the CSI subcarrier layout changed during the step")
            self._finish_step()
            return
        sd.t_last = frame.ts
        sd.last_quality = {"ok": bool(frame.quality_ok), "reasons": list(frame.quality_reasons)}
        if frame.ts - sd.t0 < sd.settle_s:
            return  # analysis window still contains data from before the step
        sd.total += 1
        feats = (frame.motion_score, frame.variance, frame.diff_energy, frame.baseline_deviation)
        if frame.quality_ok and frame.variance is not None and frame.diff_energy is not None:
            sd.ok += 1
            for name, val in zip(FEATURES, feats):
                sd.features[name].append(val)
            if profile is not None and layout is not None and np.size(profile) == layout[1]:
                sd.profiles.append(np.array(profile, dtype=float))
        else:
            for r in frame.quality_reasons or ["features unavailable"]:
                sd.reasons[r.split(":", 1)[0]] += 1
        if sd.elapsed_s >= sd.duration_s:
            self._finish_step()

    def check_timeout(self, source_ended: bool = False) -> None:
        """Wall-clock guard: end a step that receives no (or too little) data."""
        self.tick()
        if self.state != "recording":
            return
        sd = self.current
        waited = self.clock() - (sd.wall_start if sd.wall_start is not None else self.clock())
        if source_ended or waited > 2.0 * sd.duration_s + 15.0:
            sd.problems.append("the data source ended" if source_ended else "timed out waiting for data")
            self._finish_step()

    def _finish_step(self) -> None:
        sd = self.current
        problems = step_problems(sd, self.frame_rate_hz)
        if problems:
            sd.status = "failed"
            sd.failure = "; ".join(problems)
            self.state = "ready"          # redo the same step
            self._end_run()
            return
        sd.status = "done"
        sd.failure = None
        self._advance()
        nxt = self.current
        if self.running and self.auto and self.state == "ready" and nxt is not None and nxt.key in self.run_keys:
            prev, spec = STEP_BY_KEY[sd.key], STEP_BY_KEY[nxt.key]
            if spec.person_present and not prev.person_present and self.grace_s > 0:
                self._schedule(self.grace_s, "grace")
            else:
                self._schedule(0.0, "chain", t0_hint=sd.t_last)   # back to back in packet time
        elif self.state != "recording":
            self._end_run()

    def _end_run(self) -> None:
        self.running = False
        self.wait_until = None
        self.wait_kind = None

    def _advance(self) -> None:
        pending = [i for i, k in enumerate(STEP_KEYS) if self.steps[k].status != "done"]
        if pending:
            self.step_index = pending[0]
            self.state = "ready"
            return
        self.step_index = len(STEPS)
        try:
            self.compute()
        except CalibrationError:
            pass  # state 'failed' with the reasons in self.error

    def compute(self) -> dict:
        try:
            self.result = compute_calibration(self.steps, self.placement, self.frame_rate_hz, self.defaults,
                                              now=self.clock())
        except CalibrationError as e:
            self.result = None
            self.error = str(e)
            self.state = "failed"
            raise
        self.error = None
        self.state = "computed"
        return self.result

    def cancel_step(self) -> None:
        if self.state not in ("recording", "waiting"):
            raise CalibrationError("no step is being recorded")
        sd = self.current
        self.steps[sd.key] = StepData(sd.key, sd.duration_s)
        self.state = "ready"
        self._end_run()

    def redo(self, key: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        if self.state == "cancelled":
            raise CalibrationError("calibration was cancelled; start a new one")
        if self.state in ("recording", "waiting"):

    def __init__(self, engine, store: Optional[CalibrationStore] = None, auto_load: bool = True,
                 clock=time.time) -> None:

        self.session: Optional[CalibrationSession] = None

    # ----------------------------------------------------- engine thread
    def _on_frame(self, frame, activity) -> None:
        eng = self.engine
        sensor = eng.sensor_config()
        synthetic = bool(eng.synthetic)
        proc = eng.processor
        profile = proc.last_smoothed
        layout = proc.layout
        with self._lock:
            marker = (eng.started_at, sensor_part(sensor, synthetic))
            if self.auto_load and marker != self._seen and marker[1] is not None:
                self._seen = marker

                    self._auto_select(sensor, synthetic)
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - never break acquisition

                                       sensor=sensor, synthetic=synthetic, source_kind=eng.source_kind)

        match = self.store.find_match(sensor, synthetic, placement=self.placement)
        current = self.engine.calibration_info
        if match is not None:
            if current is None or current.get("key") != match["key"]:
                self._apply(match, auto=True)
                self.last_auto = {"time": self.clock(), "action": "loaded", "key": match["key"]}
            return
        if current is not None:
            if current.get("sensor_part") != sensor_part(sensor, synthetic) or bool(current.get("synthetic")) != synthetic:
                self.engine.clear_calibration()
                self.last_auto = {"time": self.clock(), "action": "cleared", "key": current.get("key"),
                                  "reason": "the active calibration does not match the detected sensor configuration"}
                return
        self.last_auto = {"time": self.clock(), "action": "none", "key": None}

    def _apply(self, data: dict, auto: bool = False) -> None:
        b = data.get("baseline") or {}
        mean, std = _to_array(b.get("mean_profile") or []), _to_array(b.get("std_profile") or [])
        if mean.size == 0 or mean.shape != std.shape:
            raise CalibrationError("calibration file has no valid baseline profile")
        th = data.get("thresholds") or {}

        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            raise CalibrationError("calibration file has no valid thresholds") from None

                "sensor_part": sensor_part(data.get("sensor"), bool(data.get("synthetic", False)))}

I'm also noticing a real bug: StepData lacks a default t_last attribute, though elapsed_s short-circuits safely when t0 is None. Now pivoting to the real design question—how to distinguish sitting from standing using CSI amplitude. The plan is to use calibration profiles per posture (walking, standing_still, sitting) and classify the current smoothed profile against these references using normalized nearest-centroid distance, combined with a motion-level gate to separate moving states from static ones.

I'm also sketching hysteresis and transition logic so posture changes require either a motion burst or sustained evidence, plus a sitting tracker state machine that accumulates streaks and triggers stand reminders similar to Apple Watch's stand-hour concept. For persistence, I'm considering daily JSONL logs or a SQLite database of posture intervals, with exportable CSV/JSON health reports (not actual transmission to providers) and a privacy disclaimer flagged clearly.

On the Wi-Fi question, the user envisions boards connecting to the home network rather than relying on ESP-NOW, which raises whether to switch to a router-mode firmware like csi_recv_router. That's a bigger change than the verified ESP-NOW setup, so I'm leaning toward keeping ESP-NOW as the default working path while treating router mode as an optional, clearly-unverified addition.

For the web app itself, I should keep it bound to localhost by default rather than exposing it on the LAN without authentication, with an opt-in flag for anyone who wants phone access. Stepping back, the core deliverables are: finishing the timing calibration sequence, pivoting the app to track sitting/standing, surfacing stand reminders and health info, logging data that's exportable for health providers, tuning detection accuracy, and keeping the website visually minimal with no gradients and a basic dashboard.

On the detection side, I'm weighing whether to touch the firmware itself — enabling HT-LTF could expand the subcarrier count well beyond the current 52 LLTF subcarriers, which might sharpen the sitting-versus-standing discrimination, but that means reflashing and extending the parser, so it's risky enough that I'd gate it behind an optional config rather than making it the default.

I think I'll leave firmware alone for now and treat that as a future enhancement, though I want to check the receiver's Kconfig to see if an HT-LTF toggle already exists. The transmitter's 100 Hz rate seems fine as is.

Now I'm sketching the feature breakdown: a first chore-type feature for baseline environment verification, folding in small fixes like the calibration timestamp bug, and a second feature redesigning the calibration timeline itself — walking the user through leaving the room for an empty baseline, a grace period on return, then walking, standing still, and sitting phases.

    """Instantiate ``dc_type`` from a dict, ignoring unknown keys and keeping
    defaults for missing or wrongly typed values."""
    obj = dc_type()

    for f in fields(dc_type):
        if f.name not in data:
            continue
        default = getattr(obj, f.name)
        value = data[f.name]
        try:
            if isinstance(default, bool):
                if isinstance(value, bool):
                    setattr(obj, f.name, value)
            elif isinstance(default, int):
                setattr(obj, f.name, int(value))
            elif isinstance(default, float):
                setattr(obj, f.name, float(value))
            else:
                setattr(obj, f.name, value)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    return obj

"""Start the EchoGuard dashboard.

    python -m dashboard                         # 127.0.0.1:8050, opens the browser
    python -m dashboard --serial auto           # start reading the receiver immediately
    python -m dashboard --replay tests/fixtures/classic_esp32s3_sample.txt --no-browser
    python -m dashboard --simulate demo         # SYNTHETIC data, no ESP32 needed

The dashboard has no authentication. It binds to 127.0.0.1 unless --host is
given; binding elsewhere exposes it to everyone on that network.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import sys
import threading
import webbrowser
from pathlib import Path

from backend.config import DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH, AppConfig
from backend.engine import Engine
from backend.sources import ReplaySource, SerialSource
from simulation.generator import SCENARIOS, SimParams, SimulationSource

from .server import create_app

LOCAL_HOSTS = {"127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"}
DISCLAIMER = "Research prototype. Not a medical device. Predictions are not medically validated."


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m dashboard", description="EchoGuard local dashboard")
    p.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1", help="bind address (default 127.0.0.1; no authentication!)")
    p.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8050, help="HTTP port (default 8050)")
    p.add_argument("--no-browser", action="store_true", help="do not open a browser window")
    src = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    src.add_argument("--serial", metavar="auto|PATH", help="start reading this serial port ('auto' to detect)")
    src.add_argument("--replay", metavar="PATH", help="start replaying a recording CSV or raw serial log")
    src.add_argument("--simulate", metavar="SCENARIO", choices=sorted(SCENARIOS),
                     help="start the SYNTHETIC simulation (" + ", ".join(SCENARIOS) + ")")
    p.add_argument("--baud", type=int, default=921600, help="serial baud rate (default 921600)")
    p.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=1.0, help="replay speed factor (0 = as fast as possible)")
    p.add_argument("--loop", action="store_true", help="loop the replay")
    p.add_argument("--config", default=str(DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH), help="config JSON (created with defaults if missing)")
    return p


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    # The UI polls several times per second; keep the per-request access log quiet.
    logging.getLogger("werkzeug").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    if not (0 < args.port < 65536):
        print("--port must be 1..65535", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    try:
        cfg = AppConfig.load_or_create(args.config)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"WARNING: could not load config {args.config} ({e}); using defaults.", file=sys.stderr)
        cfg = AppConfig()

    engine = Engine(cfg)
    app = create_app(engine, config_path=Path(args.config))

    if args.simulate:
        engine.start(SimulationSource(SimParams(scenario=args.simulate)))
        print(f"SIMULATION '{args.simulate}': synthetic data, not evidence of real-world accuracy.")
    elif args.replay:
        path = Path(args.replay)
        if not (path.is_file() or (path / "session.json").is_file()):
            print(f"Replay file or session directory not found: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        try:
            source = ReplaySource(path, speed=args.speed, loop=args.loop)
        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
            print(f"Cannot replay {path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        engine.start(source)
        print(f"Replaying {path} (recorded data, not live hardware).")
    elif args.serial:
        engine.start(SerialSource(args.serial, baud=args.baud))
        print(f"Reading serial port '{args.serial}' at {args.baud} baud (read-only).")

    url_host = args.host if args.host not in ("0.0.0.0", "::") else "127.0.0.1"
    if ":" in url_host:
        url_host = f"[{url_host}]"
    url = f"http://{url_host}:{args.port}/"
    print(f"EchoGuard dashboard: {url}")
    print(DISCLAIMER)
    if args.host not in LOCAL_HOSTS:
        print(f"WARNING: binding to {args.host}. The dashboard has NO authentication; anyone who can reach "
              f"this address can view data and change the data source. Use only on a trusted network.",
              file=sys.stderr)
    if not args.no_browser:
        threading.Timer(1.0, webbrowser.open, args=(url,)).start()
    try:
        app.run(host=args.host, port=args.port, threaded=True, debug=False, use_reloader=False)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        app.config["RECORDING"].close()
        engine.stop()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Since sitting and standing still both produce identical displacement baselines, I need to add a static posture offset to distinguish them in simulation—sitting lowers the body and changes multipath differently than standing. I'm thinking about adding an "office" or "sit_stand_day" scenario with long sitting bouts and occasional stands, possibly on an accelerated time scale for demo purposes.

Making the reminder threshold configurable from 1-180 minutes with a default of 30 so demos can show the stand reminder quickly. Now I'm settling on calibration timeline defaults: 5-second grace periods for both leaving and returning to the room, 3-second transitions between posture steps (walking to chair, standing to sitting), and a 1-second settle window at each step start. For posture optimization durations, I'm leaning toward roughly 20 seconds empty, 15 seconds walking, and 20 seconds each for standing still and sitting.

Totaling the timeline comes to about 95 seconds, roughly 1 minute 35 seconds, accounting for the grace periods, transitions, settle windows, and step durations. I'm keeping the calibration simple with just one round of sit/stand rather than adding a second round at a different spot.

For the posture classification model, I'm designing it to use per-subcarrier statistics across standing, sitting, and empty baseline classes, selecting the most discriminative subcarriers via a Fisher score comparing class means and variances, then classifying using a nearest-centroid distance over a short averaging window with a self-check validation split.

I'm also handling the "away/empty" class by comparing distance to the empty baseline centroid, with a known limitation that a still person far from the sensor could get misclassified as away. For live classification, I'm building a PostureClassifier that checks signal quality and motion first, then computes log-likelihoods for sitting, standing, and away states, applying softmax and hysteresis-based smoothing so the displayed posture only switches when the new state's probability stays above threshold for a minimum duration.

Now I'm designing the sitting tracker: accumulating separate durations for sitting, standing, and moving, defining "upright" as standing plus moving, tracking the current sitting streak, and triggering stand reminders after a configurable sitting threshold that clears once the user has been upright long enough. I'm also adding stand-hours tracking, sit-to-stand transition counts, and a log of state bouts with start/end timestamps.

Gaps of unknown or away data shouldn't count toward streaks unless prolonged—short unknown gaps under 10 seconds don't break a sitting streak, but being away for over 2 minutes does. I'm deciding that only live packet timestamps get persisted to the health log, while simulated or replayed data stays in-memory and clearly labeled so it never pollutes the stored history, keeping the database clean for real provider data. <file name="/Users/christopherryan/Projects/Hackathon/backend/posture.py" language="python" >
<content>
"""Sitting vs standing posture model built from calibration amplitude profiles.

Pure numpy (no scikit-learn). The inputs are the smoothed, mean-normalised
amplitude profiles (``SignalProcessor.last_smoothed``, one per good motion
frame) recorded during the calibration steps ``sitting``, ``standing_still``
and ``empty_baseline``. A person sitting or standing at a fixed spot changes
the static multipath pattern, so the per-subcarrier profile shifts.

Model (:func:`fit_posture_model`): per class and per subcarrier the mean and
std (std floored at :data:`backend.processing.STD_FLOOR`), a Fisher score per
subcarrier between sitting and standing
(``|mu_sit - mu_stand| / sqrt(var_sit + var_stand)``) and the indices of the
``k`` most discriminative subcarriers. :func:`score_profile` evaluates a
diagonal Gaussian log-likelihood over the selected subcarriers (non-finite
entries are ignored), :func:`classify_profile` turns it into a label and
softmax probabilities.

:func:`temporal_self_check` trains on one half of each step and tests on the
other half (both ways) using 2 s block averages. It is a within-calibration
self-check: optimistic, not a validated accuracy. The model is a location
dependent heuristic reference, not a medical measurement.

Models are plain JSON-compatible dicts (lists, ``None`` for non-finite
values), so they can be stored in calibration files and reused by other
components without conversion.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import warnings
from typing import Iterable, Optional

import numpy as np

from .processing import STD_FLOOR

MODEL_KIND = "diagonal-gaussian"
MODEL_FORMAT = 1
#: Posture classes, in display order.
CLASSES = ("sitting", "standing", "empty")
#: The two classes the subcarrier selection discriminates.
SIT_STAND = ("sitting", "standing")
#: Calibration step key -> posture class.
STEP_CLASSES = {"sitting": "sitting", "standing_still": "standing", "empty_baseline": "empty"}
DEFAULT_K = 16
SELF_CHECK_BLOCK_S = 2.0
SELF_CHECK_LABEL = "within-calibration self-check, optimistic, not a validated accuracy"
#: Warn below these values.
MIN_SELF_CHECK_ACCURACY = 0.8
MIN_FISHER = 1.0
SIMILAR_WARNING = ("sitting and standing look similar at this placement; move the boards so the line between "
                   "them passes near the chair at seated torso height, then recalibrate")
_LOG_2PI = math.log(2.0 * math.pi)


def json_list(arr) -> list:
    """Float list rounded to 6 decimals, ``None`` for non-finite values."""
    return [round(float(v), 6) if v is not None and math.isfinite(v) else None for v in np.asarray(arr, dtype=float)]


def _to_array(values) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.array([np.nan if v is None else v for v in values], dtype=float)


def _stack(profiles, name: str) -> np.ndarray:
    rows = [np.asarray(p, dtype=float).ravel() for p in profiles]
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError(f"no profiles for class '{name}'")
    widths = {r.size for r in rows}
    if len(widths) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"profiles of class '{name}' have different lengths")
    return np.vstack(rows)


def _ordered(classes: Iterable[str]) -> list:
    classes = list(classes)
    return [c for c in CLASSES if c in classes] + [c for c in classes if c not in CLASSES]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- fit
def fit_posture_model(profiles_by_class: dict, k: int = DEFAULT_K, std_floor: float = STD_FLOOR) -> dict:
    """Per-class diagonal Gaussian over the ``k`` subcarriers that best
    separate sitting from standing.

    ``profiles_by_class`` maps class names (``sitting`` and ``standing`` are
    required, ``empty`` optional) to sequences of 1-D profiles of equal length.
    Raises :class:`ValueError` for missing classes or inconsistent shapes.
    """
    if not isinstance(profiles_by_class, dict):
        raise ValueError("profiles_by_class must be a dict")
    for name in SIT_STAND:
        if len(profiles_by_class.get(name) or []) < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"need at least 2 profiles for class '{name}'")
    k = int(k)
    if k < 1:
        raise ValueError("k must be at least 1")
    names = _ordered(n for n, p in profiles_by_class.items() if p is not None and len(p) > 0)
    means, stds, counts = {}, {}, {}
    width = None
    for name in names:
        P = _stack(profiles_by_class[name], name)
        if width is None:
            width = P.shape[1]
        elif P.shape[1] != width:
            raise ValueError("profiles of different classes have different lengths")
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            mu = np.nanmean(P, axis=0)
            sd = np.nanstd(P, axis=0)
        means[name] = mu
        stds[name] = np.maximum(sd, std_floor)       # NaN stays NaN
        counts[name] = int(P.shape[0])
    mu_s, mu_t = means["sitting"], means["standing"]
    var = stds["sitting"] ** 2 + stds["standing"] ** 2
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        fisher = np.abs(mu_s - mu_t) / np.sqrt(var)
    finite = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(fisher))
    order = finite[np.argsort(-fisher[finite], kind="stable")]
    selected = [int(i) for i in order[:k]]
    return {
        "kind": MODEL_KIND,
        "format": MODEL_FORMAT,
        "classes": names,
        "n_subcarriers": int(width),
        "means": {n: json_list(means[n]) for n in names},
        "stds": {n: json_list(stds[n]) for n in names},
        "counts": counts,
        "fisher": json_list(fisher),
        "selected": selected,
        "k": len(selected),
        "best_fisher": round(float(fisher[selected[0]]), 6) if selected else None,
        "std_floor": std_floor,
    }


def validate_model(model) -> dict:
    """Check the structure of a (possibly loaded) model; returns it or raises ValueError."""
    if not isinstance(model, dict) or model.get("kind") != MODEL_KIND:
        raise ValueError("not a posture model")
    try:
        width = int(model["n_subcarriers"])
        classes = list(model["classes"])
        selected = [int(i) for i in model["selected"]]
        for c in classes:
            if len(model["means"][c]) != width or len(model["stds"][c]) != width:
                raise ValueError(f"class '{c}' has the wrong number of subcarriers")
    except (KeyError, TypeError) as e:
        raise ValueError(f"posture model is incomplete: {e}") from None
    if not all(c in classes for c in SIT_STAND):
        raise ValueError("posture model needs the sitting and standing classes")
    if not selected or any(not (0 <= i < width) for i in selected):
        raise ValueError("posture model has invalid subcarrier indices")
    return model


# ------------------------------------------------------------------- score
def score_profile(model: dict, profile, classes: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None) -> dict:
    """Diagonal Gaussian log-likelihood per class over the selected subcarriers.

    Only subcarriers that are finite in the profile and in every scored class
    are used, so the values are comparable between classes. Returns ``{}``
    when no selected subcarrier is usable. Raises :class:`ValueError` when the
    profile length differs from the model.
    """
    if profile is None:
        x = np.array([])
    elif isinstance(profile, np.ndarray):
        x = profile.astype(float).ravel()
    else:
        x = _to_array(list(profile))
    width = int(model["n_subcarriers"])
    if x.size != width:
        raise ValueError(f"profile has {x.size} subcarriers, the posture model expects {width}")
    names = list(model["classes"]) if classes is None else [c for c in classes if c in model["classes"]]
    if not names:
        return {}
    idx = np.asarray(model["selected"], dtype=int)
    xs = x[idx]
    mus = {c: _to_array(model["means"][c])[idx] for c in names}
    sds = {c: _to_array(model["stds"][c])[idx] for c in names}
    mask = np.isfinite(xs)
    for c in names:
        mask &= np.isfinite(mus[c]) & np.isfinite(sds[c]) & (sds[c] > 0)
    if not mask.any():
        return {}
    out = {}
    for c in names:
        z = (xs[mask] - mus[c][mask]) / sds[c][mask]
        out[c] = float(np.sum(-0.5 * z * z - np.log(sds[c][mask]) - 0.5 * _LOG_2PI))
    return out


def classify_profile(model: dict, profile, classes: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None):
    """``(label, {class: probability})`` via a softmax of the log-likelihoods;
    ``(None, {})`` when the profile has no usable selected subcarrier."""
    ll = score_profile(model, profile, classes)
    if not ll:
        return None, {}
    names = list(ll)
    v = np.array([ll[c] for c in names], dtype=float)
    p = np.exp(v - v.max())
    p /= p.sum()
    probs = {c: float(pi) for c, pi in zip(names, p)}
    return max(probs, key=probs.get), probs


# -------------------------------------------------------------- self-check
def block_average(profiles, block_n: int) -> list:
    """NaN-safe means of consecutive blocks of ``block_n`` profiles (full blocks
    only; all profiles as one block when there are fewer than ``block_n``)."""
    rows = list(profiles)
    if not rows:
        return []
    block_n = max(1, int(block_n))
    chunks = [rows[i:i + block_n] for i in range(0, len(rows) - block_n + 1, block_n)] or [rows]
    out = []
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
        for chunk in chunks:
            out.append(np.nanmean(np.vstack([np.asarray(r, dtype=float) for r in chunk]), axis=0))
    return out


def _tally(results: dict) -> dict:
    per = {}
    tot = cor = 0
    for c, (n, ok) in results.items():
        per[c] = {"blocks": n, "correct": ok, "accuracy": round(ok / n, 4) if n else None}
        tot += n
        cor += ok
    return {"per_class": per, "accuracy": round(cor / tot, 4) if tot else None, "blocks": tot}


def temporal_self_check(profiles_by_class: dict, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0, k: int = DEFAULT_K,
                        block_s: float = SELF_CHECK_BLOCK_S, std_floor: float = STD_FLOOR) -> dict:
    """Temporal split: fit on the first half of each class, test 2 s block
    averages of the second half, and vice versa.

    Returns accuracy per class and overall for all classes, and for the
    sitting-vs-standing decision alone (``sit_stand``). Labelled as a
    within-calibration self-check (optimistic, not a validated accuracy).
    """
    block_n = max(1, int(round(float(frame_rate_hz) * float(block_s))))
    out = {"label": SELF_CHECK_LABEL,
           "method": f"temporal split (first half / second half of each step, both ways), "
                     f"{block_s:g} s block averages",
           "block_s": block_s, "block_frames": block_n, "available": False, "reason": None}
    names = _ordered(n for n, p in profiles_by_class.items() if p is not None and len(p) > 0)
    halves = {}
    for n in names:
        rows = list(profiles_by_class[n])
        if len(rows) < 4:
            out["reason"] = f"too few profiles for class '{n}' ({len(rows)}, need 4)"
            return out
        mid = len(rows) // 2
        halves[n] = (rows[:mid], rows[mid:])
    if not all(n in halves for n in SIT_STAND):
        out["reason"] = "sitting and standing profiles are required"
        return out
    every = {n: [0, 0] for n in names}
    pair = {n: [0, 0] for n in SIT_STAND}
    for train_i, test_i in ((0, 1), (1, 0)):
        model = fit_posture_model({n: h[train_i] for n, h in halves.items()}, k=k, std_floor=std_floor)
        for n, h in halves.items():
            for block in block_average(h[test_i], block_n):
                label, _ = classify_profile(model, block)
                every[n][0] += 1
                every[n][1] += int(label == n)
                if n in pair:
                    label2, _ = classify_profile(model, block, SIT_STAND)
                    pair[n][0] += 1
                    pair[n][1] += int(label2 == n)
    allc = _tally(every)
    out.update(available=True, per_class=allc["per_class"], overall_accuracy=allc["accuracy"],
               blocks=allc["blocks"], chance_accuracy=round(1.0 / len(names), 4),
               sit_stand={**_tally(pair), "chance_accuracy": 0.5})
    return out


def quality_warnings(model: dict) -> list:
    """Warnings when sitting and standing are hard to tell apart."""
    out = []
    best = model.get("best_fisher")
    sc = model.get("self_check") or {}
    acc = (sc.get("sit_stand") or {}).get("accuracy") if sc.get("available") else None
    reasons = []
    if acc is not None and acc < MIN_SELF_CHECK_ACCURACY:
        reasons.append(f"sitting-vs-standing self-check {acc:.0%} (below {MIN_SELF_CHECK_ACCURACY:.0%}; "
                       "within-calibration, optimistic)")
    if best is None or best < MIN_FISHER:
        reasons.append(f"best subcarrier Fisher score {best if best is not None else 0:.2f} (below {MIN_FISHER:g})")
    if reasons:
        out.append(f"{SIMILAR_WARNING} ({'; '.join(reasons)})")
    if sc and not sc.get("available"):
        out.append(f"posture self-check unavailable: {sc.get('reason')}")
    return out

FEAT-003 is complete. The backend now tracks sitting and standing live, and there is a synthetic `desk_day` scenario where sitting and standing look different, so the app can be demoed without hardware. `make test` exits 0 (311 passed, 2 skipped because sklearn isn't installed) and compileall is clean. Nothing was committed. I ran `git add -N` on the new files, and `dashboard/static/*` is unchanged.

**What was built**
- **Settings:** a new `PostureConfig` in `backend/config.py` with all the planned defaults. Out-of-range values in `config.json` are clamped when it loads.
- **Classifier:** `PostureClassifier` in `backend/posture.py` labels each frame sitting, standing, moving, away or unknown.
  - It averages the profile over 3 s and waits 5 s before switching to a new still posture, or 2 s if movement just ended.
  - With no calibration it only reports moving or unknown (reason "not calibrated"). It never reports sitting or standing without a posture model.
- **Tracking, storage and service:** all in the new `backend/sitting.py`.
  - The tracker records bouts, the current sitting streak, sit-to-stand counts, stand hours (upright = standing + moving), and reminders that can be cleared or snoozed.
  - The SQLite store at `data/posture.sqlite3` only saves live, non-synthetic data. It survives a restart (tested), and the database file is in `.gitignore`.
  - A service hooks into the engine, adds a `posture` key to `/api/status`, and resets when the data source changes.
- **New routes:** `/api/posture`, `/today`, `/history`, `/settings` (GET and POST, saved to `config.json`), `/reminder/snooze` and `/export` (CSV or JSON download with the disclaimer header). Bad dates, day counts, formats and settings all return 400.
- **Simulator:** sitting and standing now produce different signals, and the `desk_day` scenario runs about 5 minutes with 75 s and 90 s sitting bouts. The fall-detection modules, routes and tests still pass.

**Decisions to review**
- **Added `POST /api/simulation/calibrate`:** this wasn't in the plan. The real timed calibration can't line up with the `desk_day` script, so without this route the demo can never show sitting or standing. It builds and applies a synthetic calibration in about 3 s and returns 400 unless the simulation is running. To support it, `CalibrationManager.save_result()` was added and `save()` now uses it.
- **Fixed simulated room:** the simulated room is now the same on every run, so one synthetic calibration keeps working for later simulation runs. The seed now only changes the noise.
- **Short movements:** movement has to last 1 s before it replaces a still posture, so fidgeting while seated stays "sitting".
- **Streak and reminder state:** this lives in memory and resets on restart; only bouts and reminder records are saved.

**Verification**
- An automated test calibrates on the simulator, then runs `desk_day`. Well inside each segment, sitting reads "sitting", standing and walking read "standing" or "moving", and the empty room reads "away". `/api/posture` is labelled synthetic, and nothing is written to SQLite.

- Live hardware is not verified, because the sandbox can't open serial ports.
